summary: TaiYouWeb/ra2 is an unchanged GitHub fork of ra2-games/ra2 ("RA2 VM", live at https://ra2.games). It is not a reimplementation of RA2 and not a Chrono Divide derivative. It runs EA's original x86 executables (game.exe from RA2 1.006, gamemd.exe from YR 1.001) inside the browser. It does this with the v86 x86 emulator (JIT to WASM, 0.5.441), a custom 64 KB firmware (src/vm86/boot.asm), its own PE loader, and a TypeScript reimplementation of the Win32, DirectDraw, DirectSound, Winsock/IPX and DirectPlay APIs. No Windows is booted. The fork has 0 commits of its own and is 9 commits (93 files, +5130/-242) behind upstream. The owner, TaiYouWeb, has 56 public repos, 54 of them forks, so this looks like a bookmark fork. Build is VERIFIED: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile, then pnpm run build, finished in about 11 s with exit 0. The 803 asset-free unit tests in 115 files also pass. Because it runs the real engine, gameplay fidelity is potentially perfect: real AI, real lockstep netcode, campaigns, FMVs through the guest Binkw32.dll, and EVA/music. That fits Step 1 well. It is structurally very poor for Step 2. The game draws everything with its own software blitter into a DirectDraw surface in emulated memory, and JavaScript only receives the finished 8-bit indexed, RGB565 or RGBA frame. The only HD levers today are whole-frame post-processing: Anime4K CNN/GAN, FSR1, ScaleFX, bicubic, and a SweetFX vibrance+sharpen port. HD sprites, voxel meshes, water shaders and depth-correct weather would all need reverse-engineered render hooks in the proprietary binary. The repo's own docs/RESHADE_ADAPTATION.md lists these as not implemented. There is also a serious legal problem. The app does not use the player's own executable. It automatically fetches EA's copyrighted game.exe/gamemd.exe from a third-party host, and its UI links to unofficial full-game download sites.
license_evidence: LICENSE is the full GNU GPL v3 text ("GNU GENERAL PUBLIC LICENSE / Version 3, 29 June 2007"). package.json: "license": "GPL-3.0-or-later". README: "Original project code is **GPL-3.0-or-later**". GitHub API reports spdx_id GPL-3.0 for both the fork and the upstream ra2-games/ra2. docs/THIRD_PARTY.md says game files ("game.exe, gamemd.exe, MIX files, maps, audio, and video") are "Outside this project's GPL code". It also says the launcher background image has no asset license ("GPL must not be presumed"). Bundled third-party code: v86 is BSD-2-Clause (node_modules/v86/package.json "license": "BSD-2-Clause"); LZMA-JS, Anime4K shaders, SweetFX (src/graphics/vendor/sweetfx/LICENSE), FSR1 and ScaleFX are MIT. Legal caveat: the code license is clean, but the runtime depends on EA-proprietary binaries. src/games/manifest.ts hardcodes url 'https://oldgame.store/game.exe' (sha256 06f99496…) and 'https://oldgame.store/gamemd.exe' (sha256 7b8a0685…). A HEAD request to the latter on 2026-09-27 returned HTTP 200, application/x-msdownload, 4,813,072 bytes, CORS *. src/adapter/thirdPartyFiles.ts fetches these in production and caches them in IndexedDB. In src/ui/pages/game/gameSourcePicker.ts:121 the downloaded exe overlays the player's files, so the player's own exe is never used. src/games/downloadCatalog.ts links to uc129.com, jb51.net and archive.org full-game installers. EA's Feb-2025 GPL source release covered Tiberian Dawn, Red Alert 1, Renegade and Generals, not RA2 (https://www.engadget.com/gaming/pc/ea-releases-source-code-for-four-command--conquer-games-223425774.html). RA2/YR code and assets therefore remain EA-proprietary.
provenance: Fork of ra2-games/ra2 with zero unique commits. The upstream is original work: a v86-based Win32/DirectX compatibility layer that runs EA's original binaries. It is NOT derived from Chrono Divide and NOT a decompile of RA2 or Chrono Divide.
provenance_evidence: VERIFIED: the GitHub API shows fork:true, with parent and source both ra2-games/ra2. The fork was created 2026-09-14 and last pushed 2026-09-18. Its three commits (5758256 empty "init" 2026-09-13; aa1eef8 "init OSS release" 2026-09-14 with 454 files and +82,414 lines; 4838445 2026-09-17) are byte-identical to upstream: same commit SHAs and tree SHAs. `gh api compare` reports upstream ahead by 9 and the fork ahead by 0. All three commits are authored by "agent <agent@anonymous.local>". AGENTS.md (with CLAUDE.md symlinked to it) says internal work happens on a private `dev` branch "never push dev to GitHub". The public history is therefore one squashed dump, and the real development history is hidden. That is a transparency concern, but the architecture makes a stolen-engine scenario implausible. There is no game-simulation code at all: grep finds no SHP/VXL/HVA/TMP/MIX/CSF parsers and no Three.js. The only asset-type mention is a file-extension regex in src/games/shared/resourcePolicy.ts. All game logic runs inside the original EXE under emulation. The code reads as original engineering: src/vm86/* shims, NASM firmware, fixed-address patches with SHA-256 plus instruction-signature guards in src/games/{ra2,yr}/*, and reverse-engineering helpers in scripts/reverse/*. The only "Chrono Divide" mentions are CSS comments in src/ui/pages/game/styles.css (lines 576, 998, 1018, 1527, 2087) saying the web UI styling references Chrono Divide's message-box, slider-item and select CSS. That is minor UI-style borrowing, possibly copied CSS patterns (INFERENCE, not verified). It has nothing in common with DD-Channel/ra2-web, OpenRA2/RA2Web or huangkaoya/ts-redalert2, which are TypeScript reimplementations; their histories (huangkaoya authors, 2025–2026) differ entirely. The project appears largely AI-agent-built (.agents/skills, AGENTS.md rules). Game .exe files come from oldgame.store, not from the player (see license_evidence).
tech_stack: TypeScript 5.9, React 19.3 for web UI only, Vite 6.4, Vitest 4.1, Playwright 1.60, pnpm 11.24.0 (strict packageManager/engines), Node (unpinned; built fine on Node v26.0.0). Runtime deps: v86 0.5.441 (x86 emulator, WASM JIT), 7z-wasm 1.2.0 and fflate for archive import (ZIP/7z/RAR/NSIS installers, plus a vendored LZMA-JS), onnxruntime-web 1.29.0 (dev-only experimental SR models on WebGPU), qrcode. The firmware is NASM assembly (src/vm86/boot.asm → boot.bin). The multiplayer relay is a separate Node WebSocket server (packages/relay, ws, Docker compose) that uses its own binary wire protocol. Rendering uses raw WebGL2 with hand-written GLSL, falling back to Canvas2D, with no 3D engine. Source is about 44k lines under src/ and packages/, including a 2.7k-line vendored LZMA worker and about 1.2k lines of Anime4K GLSL.
renderer_architecture: There is no RA2 asset renderer in JavaScript. The original gamemd.exe/game.exe decodes MIX/SHP/VXL/HVA/TMP/PAL/CSF/INI itself, blits with its own CPU software rasterizer, and applies house colors, palettes, lighting and voxel rasterization internally, at its native pixel scale, into DirectDraw surfaces in emulated guest memory. src/vm86/shim/directx.ts implements IDirectDraw, IDirectDrawSurface (Lock/Unlock/Blt/BltFast/Flip), IDirectDrawPalette and IDirectDrawClipper over guest memory, plus DirectSound buffers. src/vm86/shim/user32Windowing.ts composes Win32 controls into RGBA for shell menus. At DirectDraw frame boundaries the shim emits a VmFrame (src/vm86/win32.ts:101): 8-bit indexes + 256-entry PALETTEENTRY palette, or RGB565, or RGBA, plus an independent cursor bitmap. src/graphics/framePresenter.ts keeps only the newest frame. src/ui/pages/game/vmFrameRenderer.ts (WebGL2; Canvas2D fallback) uploads indexes as an R8 texture with a 256x1 palette texture and does palette lookup in a fragment shader (texelFetch), or uploads RGB565/RGBA directly. It then applies an optional upscaler before the cursor quad: bicubic, FSR1 EASU/RCAS (fsrUpscale.ts), ScaleFX 3x (scalefxUpscale.ts), or Anime4K CNN-S/GAN-M 2x in RGBA16F FBOs (aiUpscale.ts plus vendor GLSL). An optional ColorPostProcess pass (src/graphics/framePostProcess.ts, setPostProcess()) runs the SweetFX Vibrance+LumaSharpen port (src/graphics/reshadePreset.ts). src/graphics/experimental/reshadeLaser.ts is a dev-only one-pass ReShade LaserBlit experiment with no real game masks. Guest resolution is set by patching RA2.INI/RA2MD.INI [Video] ScreenWidth/Height; the presets in src/games/resolution.ts go up to 1920x1080. A higher resolution shows more map, not more detail. There is no WebGPU renderer; WebGPU is used only by the dev ONNX model probe. There is no lighting model, camera or projection on the host side; all of that is inside the EXE. Netcode is the original game's lockstep IPX/Winsock (src/games/ra2/winsock.ts, networkTransport.ts) tunneled as datagrams through a WebSocket relay (packages/relay). DirectPlay is shimmed separately (src/vm86/shim/dplayx.ts). Audio: DirectSound buffers are mixed into an AudioWorklet (src/adapter/audio.ts, pcmStreamWorklet). Video: Bink FMVs are decoded by the player-supplied x86 Binkw32.dll running inside the emulator (src/vm86/win32.ts:524-552 routes its exports).

feature_completeness:
Because the original engine executes, every gameplay feature exists in principle. The question is whether the Win32/DirectX shim is complete enough. "Code" below means the support is VERIFIED in code.
- Allied/Soviet campaigns: the manifest accepts Maps01/Maps02/movies01/02 as optional. There are campaign-menu shim compensations (src/vm86/shim/user32Windowing.ts:1642-1719, gameProfile.ts CampaignMenuCompatibility). The docs say explicitly that full campaigns are not verified: "reaching the main menu cannot prove campaign completeness" (docs/RESOURCE_PACKAGE_EVIDENCE.md).
- YR content: supported through gamemd.exe 1.001 (src/games/yr/*); boot test exists (tests/real-game/yr/boot.test.ts).
- Skirmish vs AI: original AI, 100% faithful. There is a direct-skirmish startup trampoline (src/games/shared/startupTrampoline.ts, src/games/*/startupPage.ts). Code, and in README.
- Multiplayer: original lockstep over Winsock/IPX, tunneled through a self-hosted WebSocket relay (packages/relay, src/games/ra2/winsock.ts). Code. The docs say only two-client short matches were tested; no reconnection or resumption; 8-player not established. No public matchmaking (no CnCNet/XWIS integration).
- Units, buildings, superweapons, naval/water, bridges, garrisoning, veterancy, Chronosphere/Iron Curtain, fog/shroud: all native engine behavior, so inherently present but unverified at runtime. One guard exists: repairRa2InvalidRepairRate.
- Custom maps: .yrm/.mpr (and .csf) through an archive dialog (src/adapter/customMapPackage.ts). Plain .map is not in the accepted list (code).
- Sound, EVA, music: DirectSound shim + AudioWorklet (code). Theme.mix/thememd.mix optional.
- FMV: Bink through the guest Binkw32.dll (code); required in the manifest.
- Save/load: session overlay + IndexedDB (src/adapter/saveTransfer.ts, platform/browser/files/sessionFiles.ts). Code. Upstream issue #1 reported save failure on macOS; upstream later shipped "save/load improvements" that the fork lacks.
- Replays: none (RA2/YR have no native replays; nothing added).
- INI modding: top-level rules.ini/art.ini/ai.ini overrides and the Chinese mod 共和国之辉 (Gonghui: expand01.mix/ecache01.mix/ra2.csf) are accepted (manifest.ts). Ares/Phobos/Syringe DLL mods are not supported; there is guest-DLL loading machinery, but it is used only for Binkw32.
- Map editor: none.
- High resolution: guest res presets up to 1920x1080 (src/games/resolution.ts), plus host upscalers. No FPS numbers are published; the performance docs only describe methodology. Performance is UNVERIFIED and bounded by x86 emulation plus a software blitter at 1080p.
- Also present: touch controls, keyboard lock, English/Simplified Chinese UI, and a WeChat group QR dialog.
asset_requirements:
RA2 (src/games/manifest.ts), player-supplied and required: ra2.mix, language.mix, Binkw32.dll, Blowfish.dll. Optional: Maps01.mix, Maps02.mix (campaigns), movies01.mix, movies02.mix, subtitle.txt, Theme.mix, Multi.mix, game.fnt, Taunts/, and top-level rules.ini/art.ini/ai.ini, expand01.mix/ecache01.mix/ra2.csf (Gonghui mod).
YR: ra2md.mix, langmd.mix, BINKW32.DLL, Blowfish.dll required. Optional: expandmd01.mix, MAPSMD03.MIX, movmd03.mix, subtitlemd.txt, thememd.mix, MULTIMD.MIX, game.fnt, Taunts/.
How to supply: "Select files…" for an archive (ZIP/7z/RAR, or an NSIS/SFX installer that is parsed rather than executed) or "Select folder…" for a directory. Everything is extracted in a Worker and cached in IndexedDB.
The executables game.exe (RA2 1.006, sha256 06f99496…) and gamemd.exe (YR 1.001, sha256 7b8a0685…) are NOT taken from the player. They are downloaded from oldgame.store and overlaid on the player's files. The version-specific patches are hash-locked, so an EA App/Steam "Ultimate Collection" exe with a different hash would fail the signature checks; this is INFERENCE from the hash gating in src/games/*/startupPage.ts and startupTrampoline.ts. No game files are needed to build.
hd_extensibility:
Overall this is poor for the stated HD goals. The host only ever sees finished frames; the game's world rendering is locked inside EA's binary. Per technique:
(1) Post-processing, color grading, AI/spatial upscaling: EASY, and it already exists. Plug in through VmFrameRenderer.setPostProcess() (src/ui/pages/game/vmFrameRenderer.ts:42,116) and ColorPostProcess (src/graphics/framePostProcess.ts), or the upscale modes in vmFrameRenderer.ts setUpscaleMode(), aiUpscale.ts, fsrUpscale.ts and scalefxUpscale.ts. Limits: it applies to the whole frame including the sidebar and UI (no masks). The engine's native pixel grid is fixed, so AI upscaling just enlarges 800x600–1080p pixel art, and Anime4K is tuned for animation. The dev-only ONNX models (src/ui/pages/game/experiments/*) cap at 800x600 input.
(2) Hi-res sprite/SHP replacement: VERY HARD. You would need guest code hooks at the game's draw functions (for example AnimClass/TechnoClass draw), using fixed addresses and signatures in src/games/yr/* following the installStartupTrampoline pattern (src/games/shared/startupTrampoline.ts). Draw commands would be marshalled out via the hypercall page (src/vm86/pe.ts HYPERCALL_*) into a new host-side WebGL compositor that re-renders the tactical view with HD textures. That compositor must preserve occlusion, z-order, shadows and house-color remap. docs/RESHADE_ADAPTATION.md states this bridge is "not integrated". YR 1.001 addresses are documented by community YRpp headers; RA2 1.006 has far less reverse-engineering coverage.
(3) VXL to real-time mesh: VERY HARD, the same hook problem. Intercept voxel rendering (the Toumao DLL string "TechnoClass_RenderVxl_ReplaceMesh" hints this is possible on Windows), pull VXL/HVA data and facing/turret state from guest memory, and render in host WebGL with a correct depth composite.
(4) Normal/depth-map lighting: HARD. It needs the game's Z-buffer, shroud and water masks extracted from guest memory each frame. YR has these; ReShadeK exposes ZBUFFER/WATER/SHROUD through native hooks. Only final RGB exists today (VmFrame has no auxiliary buffers).
(5) Water shader: HARD. It needs a water mask and depth plus viewport scroll from guest memory, and a composite under units.
(6) Weather and GPU particles: MEDIUM as screen-space overlays (a post-process pass). HARD to make world-correct: you would need to read the tactical viewport coordinates and object positions from memory using hash-validated fixed addresses, the pattern used in src/games/*/performance.ts, and you would still lack occlusion.
(7) Modern hit/explosion effects: HARD. Replacing the engine's SHP anims needs draw hooks, as in (2).
In short, this base gives near-perfect Step 1 fidelity but makes Step 2 a reverse-engineering project on a proprietary binary under emulation. That work is fragile and specific to one exe version, and performance headroom inside v86 is unknown.
risks: Legal and distribution: the production code auto-downloads EA-copyrighted game.exe/gamemd.exe from a third-party host (https://oldgame.store, hardcoded in src/games/manifest.ts) instead of using the player's own copy. Building a public HD product on this repeats that exposure unless the fetch is removed and the player supplies a matching exe.
Legal: the UI download catalog (src/games/downloadCatalog.ts) links to unofficial full-game installers (uc129.com, jb51.net, archive.org), which facilitates piracy.
RA2/YR remain EA-proprietary (not part of EA's 2025 GPL release). Any HD asset pack derived from the original art is a derivative work of EA assets. The GPL covers only the shim code.
Stale bookmark fork: 0 unique commits, 9 commits behind upstream, missing its fixes for long-session leaks, crashes and audio. Use ra2-games/ra2 directly if this approach is chosen.

Opaque history: squashed 'init OSS release' of about 82k lines, private dev branch never pushed, commits by 'agent@anonymous.local'. Largely AI-agent-authored, with bus factor tied to a small anonymous team. Upstream is only about 2 weeks old.

Architectural mismatch with the HD goal: rendering happens in the EXE's CPU software blitter. The host sees only final frames, so hi-res textures, voxel meshes, water, lighting and effects need reverse-engineered hooks into a proprietary binary, hash-locked to one exe version (RA2 1.006 / YR 1.001).
Exe version lock: patches validate exact SHA-256 and instruction signatures, so legitimately purchased EA App/Steam versions likely don't match (inference) and would need new per-version patch work.

Performance is unknown: x86 emulation (v86 JIT) plus a software blitter at up to 1920x1080, and no FPS numbers are published. Adding host-side re-rendering and extra memory reads per frame could hurt simulation speed.

Alpha maturity: full campaigns, long matches, 4–8 player matches and public-network reliability are explicitly unverified. There is no reconnection, and a macOS save failure was reported upstream (issue #1).
Mod ecosystem gap: no Ares/Phobos/Syringe support, which is where the modern YR rendering and extension work lives.
UI CSS styling is modeled on Chrono Divide's style.css per code comments; low risk, but verify there is no verbatim copying before redistribution.
score_rationale:
Positives: the code is GPL-3.0-or-later and is not a Chrono Divide copy. It builds and tests cleanly (build exit 0 in about 11 s, 803/803 unit tests). It offers the highest possible gameplay fidelity for Step 1 because it runs the real RA2/YR engine, including AI, lockstep netcode, campaigns, FMV, saves and INI mods. Its engineering is disciplined: hash- and signature-guarded patches, clear module boundaries, and architecture tests.
Negatives that dominate for THIS project:
(a) Step 2 is structurally blocked. All world rendering happens inside EA's proprietary binary via a software blitter, so crisp materials, voxel meshes, modern water, weather and effects need deep reverse-engineered render hooks. What exists today is only whole-frame upscaling and post-processing.
(b) The shipped runtime pulls copyrighted EA executables from an unofficial host and links to piracy sites, which is a real legal liability for anything published.
(c) This specific repo is a zero-contribution, already-stale mirror (9 commits behind), with 0 stars and issues disabled.
(d) The project is Alpha, with key features (full campaigns, 8-player, long matches) unverified, and performance headroom under emulation is unknown.
If the user chooses the emulate-the-original-exe route, the base should be upstream ra2-games/ra2 (I would rate it about 4 to 5). That route mainly gives "original RA2 in a browser plus filters", not a true 2.5D HD remaster.
